00-21.title: FIRST Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate - T1
00-21.description: FIRST Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate (T1) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. Further information can be found at the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-24.title: General Radiotelephone Operator License - PG
00-24.description: General Radiotelephone Operator License (PG) is issued for a lifetime and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-26.title: GMDSS Radio Maintainer's License - DM
00-26.description: GMDSS (Global Maritime Distress and Safety System) Radio Maintainer's License (DM) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-27.title: GMDSS Radio Operator's License - DO
00-27.description: GMDSS (Global Maritime Distress and Safety System) Radio Operator's License (DO) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-25.title: Marine Radio Operator Permit - MP
00-25.description: Marine Radio Operator Permit (MP) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-58.title: Radio Officer
00-58.description: The Radio Officer's license is issued to applicants who have a valid Federal Communications Commission (FCC) license as first or second class radiotelegraph operator (T1, T2). Certain officers are required to hold Global Maritime Distress and Safety System (GMDSS) certification issued by the FCC. Further information can be found at theUSCG website http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-58.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-75.title: Restricted Radiotelephone Operator Permit (RP)
00-75.description: RP holders are authorized to operate most aircraft and aeronautical ground stations. They can also operate marine radiotelephone stations aboard pleasure craft (other than those carrying more than six passengers for hire on the Great Lakes or bays or tidewaters or in the open sea) when operator licensing is required. To obtain this permit, you must be able to speak and hear; and keep a written log; and be familiar with provisions of applicable treaties, laws and rules which govern the radio station you will operate. For further information, see the Federal Communications web site at http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/rp.html.

00-22.title: SECOND Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate - T2
00-22.description: SECOND Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate (T2) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-23.title: THIRD Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate - T3
00-23.description: THIRD Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate (T3) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-57.title: Assistant Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels
00-57.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as an Assistant Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels include 1,080 days at sea with 720 days on Motor Vessels. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG website http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-57.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-56.title: Chief Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels
00-56.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Chief Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels include 1,440 days at sea with 360 days as a Licensed Engineer and 950 days on Motor Vessels. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm.
00-56.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-19.title: Inspector's Authorization
00-19.description: To obtain an inspector's authorization, a mechanic must have held an Aircraft Mechanic A & P certificate for at least 3 years. For further information, see web site http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ, parts 65.91-65.95.

00-41.title: Operator of Uninspected Passenger Vessels - OUPV
00-41.description: To become licensed as an Operator of Uninspected Passenger Vessels requires specific experience -- Near Coastal or Inland as well as passing a written exam. Recent training in First Aid and Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) is also required. For complete details see the USCG web page http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr13_02, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at website http://frwebgate4.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/waisgate.cgi?WAISdocID=50846230377+3+0+0&WAISaction=retrieve or http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-41.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-42.title: Operator of Uninspected Towing Vessels - OUTV
00-42.description: To become licensed as a an Operator of Uninspected Towing Vessels (OUTV) or 2nd Class Operator of Uninspected Towing Vessels (OUTV) requires specific experience - Oceans (Domestic Route), Near Coastal or Inland, as well as passing a written exam. Recent training in First Aid and Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) is also required. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Details can be found on the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-42.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

01-132.title: Licensed Elevator Inspector
01-132.description: An inspector shall meet the definition of "Elevator Personnel" in ASME A17.1/CSA B44, Section 1.3 and have documented training and at least 1 year of experience performing inspections and performing or witnessing tests specified in ASME A17.1/CSA B44, CSA B311, ASME A18.1 or CSA B355, and ANSI/ASSE A10.4 or CSA Z185. Verifiable evidence of training and experience shall be documented with the application for license to the department. Knowledge may be evidenced by approved written and/or oral examinations, as administered by the department or other organizations acceptable to the department. Applicant shall demonstrate knowledge of personal safety practices, familiarity with industry terminology, ability to read architectural and installation drawings including hoistway and machine room layouts. working knowledge of electrical, electronic, and circuit construction principles, working knowledge of mechanical principles as applied to structures, machines, mechanisms, and the effects of traction on ropes and sheaves. Understanding and working knowledge of hydraulic principles as applied to the operation of valves, pumps, plungers, piping, and buffers, and working knowledge of the various types of equipment; their code requirements, uses, and limitations. Applicant shall have working knowledge of the functions and operations of elevator systems, including machines, motors, governor…
01-132.agency: Alabama Department of Finance,Real Property Management Division of Construction Management

01-185.title: Licensed Exterior Insulation and Finishing System Inspector (EIFS)
01-185.description: An inspector shall meet the definition as established by the board. Verifiable evidence of training and experience shall be documented with the application for license to the department. Knowledge may be evidenced by approved written and/or oral examinations, as administered by the department or other organizations acceptable to the department. Applicant shall demonstrate knowledge of personal safety practices, familiarity with industry terminology, ability to read architectural and installation drawings including hoistway and machine room layouts. working knowledge of electrical, electronic, and circuit construction principles, working knowledge of mechanical principles as applied to structures, machines, mechanisms, and the effects of traction on ropes and sheaves.
01-185.agency: Alabama Department of Finance,Real Property Management Division of Construction Management

01-186.title: Licensed Home Inspector
01-186.description: An inspector shall meet the definition as established by the board. Verifiable evidence of training and experience shall be documented with the application for license to the department. Knowledge may be evidenced by approved written and/or oral examinations, as administered by the department or other organizations acceptable to the department. Applicant shall demonstrate knowledge of personal safety practices, familiarity with industry terminology, ability to read architectural and installation drawings including hoistway and machine room layouts. working knowledge of electrical, electronic, and circuit construction principles, working knowledge of mechanical principles as applied to structures, machines, mechanisms, and the effects of traction on ropes and sheaves.
01-186.agency: Alabama Department of Finance,Real Property Management Division of Construction Management

01-147.title: CDL Class B
01-147.description: This applicant should meet the minimum age requirement, depending on the license desired; Current driver license; Current DOT medical form; Transportation Security Administration background check; Proof of insurance.

01-cdl.title: Commercial Drivers License (CDL)
01-cdl.description: Commercial Drivers Licenses are issued by state departments but are similar from state to state, since the minimum requirements of the licenses and endorsements are set centrally. For more information contact the state DMV or https://cms.fmcsa.dot.gov/registration/commercial-drivers-license/how-do-i-get-commercial-drivers-license.
01-cdl.agency: Alabama Law Enforcement Agency · Driver License Division

01-3.title: Alabama Professional Leadership Certificate
01-3.description: Applicants should contact the Alabama State Department of Education licensing board for qualifications and requirements.

01-66.title: Alabama Licensed Chiropractor
01-66.description: In order to become a licensed Doctor of Chiropractic in the state of Alabama, an applicant must have a bachelor’s degree, must be a graduate of a Council on Chiropractic Education-approved college of Chiropractic (course of study varies from four to five years not including pre-chiropractic), and have passed a state jurisprudence exam, and parts of the National Board of Chiropractic Examiners.

requirements.label: Exam
requirements.value: Both state and third-party exams required

01-66.agency: Alabama State Board of Chiropractic Examiners

01-8.title: Licensed Insurance Adjuster
01-8.description: An adjuster is any person who, as an independent contractor or an employee of an independent contractor, adjustment bureau, association, insurance company or corporation, local recording agent, managing general agent, or self-insured, investigates or adjusts losses on behalf of either an insurer or a self-insured, or any person who supervises the handling of claims. Individuals must be at least 18 years of age and a citizen of the United States and submit proof. Applicants must have completed the 20 or 40 hour pre-licensing course and passed the state exam. Applicants should be fingerprinted after passing the state exam and one day before applying for the license.

01-123.title: Licensed Insurance Managing General Agent
01-123.description: Applicants must be at least 19 years of age and an Alabama resident or a full-time employee of licensed Alabama agent with principal place of business is physically located in Alabama. All agents must keep their name and address current. Applicants must have completed a 20 hour course by an approved provider.
01-123.agency: State of Alabama Department of Insurance

01-197.title: Licensed Insurance Producer
01-197.description: Applicants must be at least 19 years of age and an Alabama resident or a full-time employee of licensed Alabama agent with principal place of business is physically located in Alabama. All agents must keep their name and address current. Applicants must have completed a 20 hour course by an approved provider.
01-197.agency: State of Alabama Department of Insurance

01-198.title: Licensed Insurance Service Representative
01-198.description: Applicants must be at least 19 years of age and an Alabama resident or a full-time employee of licensed Alabama agent with principal place of business is physically located in Alabama. All agents must keep their name and address current. Applicants must have completed a 20 hour course by an approved provider.
01-198.agency: State of Alabama Department of Insurance

01-2.title: License Home Builder
01-2.description: One who engages in the construction, remodeling, repair, improvement, or reimprovement of a residential structure where the cost of the undertaking including labor and materials exceeds $10,000, unless the work performed is not within the jurisdiction of the Board.
01-2.agency: State of Alabama Home Builders Licensure Board

01-1.title: Licensed General Contractor
01-1.description: One who engages in the construction of commercial or public properties where the cost of the undertaking including labor and materials is $50,000 or more and swimming pool construction of $5,000 or more.
01-1.agency: State of Alabama Home Builders Licensure Board

01-50.title: Licensed Court Reporter
01-50.description: To become a licensed Court reporter in the State of Alabama; Applicants must provide proof of graduation from court reporting program or its equivalent in the form of: Official Transcripts, Copy of Diploma, or Official Letter from the Court Reporting Program’s Director; Pass the Licensure Examination; Complete the application and remit all appropriate fees.

requirements.label: Exam
requirements.value: Choice of state or third-party exam

01-150.title: CDL Class A
01-150.description: This applicant should meet the minimum age requirement, depending on the license desired; Current driver license; Current DOT medical form; Transportation Security Administration background check; Proof of insurance.

01-96.title: Licensed Dental Hygienist
01-96.description: The individual must be at least 19 years of age. The individual must be a graduate of a school or college of dental hygiene approved by the Alabama Board of Dental Examiners, or the individual must be a graduate of the Alabama Dental Hygiene Program (ADHP) conducted by the Alabama Board of Dental Examiners.
01-96.agency: Board of Dental Examiners of Alabama

01-72.title: Licensed Dietician
01-72.description: This applicant must be 19 years of age or older and submit evidence of good moral character and respectability; File a written application on a form provided by the board; Have satisfactorily completed appropriate academic requirements with a major course of study in human nutrition, foods and nutrition, dietetics, or food systems management, and have received a baccalaureate or higher degree from a college or university accredited by the Southern Association of Schools and Colleges or other regional accreditation agency; Have satisfactorily completed a planned, continuous pre-professional experience component in dietetics/nutrition practices of not less than 900 hours under the supervision of a registered dietitian or a practitioner licensed under the conditions of this chapter.
01-72.agency: Alabama State Board of Examiners for Dietetics/Nutrition

01-153.title: Licensed Electrical Contractor
01-153.description: Electrical contractor applicants must have four (4) years supervisory experience in commercial or industrial experience. Journeyman applicants must have Four (4) years commercial or industrial experience and may substitute two (2) years of education for one (1) year of work experience. The applicant for an electrical contractor’s license may substitute (1) year of education consisting of two (2) full time semesters or three (3) full time quarters in an approved electrical curriculum or one (1) year of an approved apprenticeship program for one thousand (1,000) hours of electrical experience. A maximum of two thousand (2,000) hours of the eight thousand (8,000) hours total requirement can be met with the substituted hours. The applicant must provide appropriate documentation of the substituted hours in an electrical curriculum or apprenticeship program, subject to the approval of the Board.

01-129.title: Licensed Journeyman Electrician
01-129.description: Persons applying for statewide Journeyman examination must demonstrate a minimum of 8,000 hours of experience that shows you have the necessary qualifications, training and technical knowledge to install electrical wiring, apparatus or equipment, light, heat or power. An applicant for a statewide Journeyman Electrician examination may substitute one year of education in an approved electrical curriculum or apprenticeship program for one thousand hours of electrical experience for a maximum of two thousand hours of the eight thousand hours total required. The applicant must provide appropriate documentation, subject to the approval of the Board, of said education or apprenticeship program.

01-180.title: Licensed Provisional Electrical Contractor
01-180.description: Persons applying for statewide Journeyman examination must demonstrate a minimum of 8,000 hours of experience that shows you have the necessary qualifications, training and technical knowledge to install electrical wiring, apparatus or equipment, light, heat or power. An applicant for a statewide Journeyman Electrician examination may substitute one year of education in an approved electrical curriculum or apprenticeship program for one thousand hours of electrical experience for a maximum of two thousand hours of the eight thousand hours total required. The applicant must provide appropriate documentation, subject to the approval of the Board, of said education or apprenticeship program.

01-196.title: Licensed Provisional Electrical Contractor
01-196.description: Electrical contractor applicants must have four (4) years supervisory experience in commercial or industrial experience. Journeyman applicants must have Four (4) years commercial or industrial experience and may substitute two (2) years of education for one (1) year of work experience. The applicant for an electrical contractor’s license may substitute (1) year of education consisting of two (2) full time semesters or three (3) full time quarters in an approved electrical curriculum or one (1) year of an approved apprenticeship program for one thousand (1,000) hours of electrical experience. A maximum of two thousand (2,000) hours of the eight thousand (8,000) hours total requirement can be met with the substituted hours. The applicant must provide appropriate documentation of the substituted hours in an electrical curriculum or apprenticeship program, subject to the approval of the Board.

01-133.title: Licensed Elevator Mechanic
01-133.description: This applicant should demonstrate An acceptable combination of documented experience and education credits: not less than 3 years work experience in the elevator industry, in construction, maintenance and service/repair, as verified by current and previous employers licensed to do business in the State of Alabama. Satisfactory completion of a written examination administered by the Division on the most recent referenced codes and standards. Certificates of completion and successfully passing the mechanic examination of a nationally recognized training program for the elevator industry such as the National Elevator Industry Educational Program or the Canadian Elevator Industry Education Program or their equivalent, that have been approved by the Department; or certificates of completion of an apprenticeship program for elevator mechanic, having standards substantially equal to those of this chapter, and registered with the Bureau of Apprenticeship and Training, U.S. Department of Labor or the Alabama Department of Labor. A license shall be issued to an individual holding a valid license from a state or province having standards substantially equal to those of this chapter, upon application and payment of the fee but without examination. A limited elevator mechanic must be certified by the manufacturer of the equipment he or she installs or an approved training program acceptabl…

01-170.title: Licensed Embalmer
01-170.description: Interested applicants should visit the Alabama Funeral Services Board for information on qualifications and requirements.

01-97.title: Registered Intermediate Emergency Medical Technician (EMT)
01-97.description: The license candidate shall be 18 years of age within 1 year of the course completion date of the entry level course. Candidate must be a high school graduate or have a GED equivalent, or have completed a high school dual enrollment course. The license candidate shall meet the essential functions of an EMSP as outlined in the Functional Job Analysis. The Functional Job Analysis was developed and adopted for the State examination accommodations to meet the requirements of the ADA. A copy of these functions may be reviewed in the U.S. Department of Transportation, National Highway Traffic Safety Administration’s Emergency Medical Technician: EMT, National Standard Curriculum: Appendix A. The license candidate shall disclose any convictions during enrollment procedures and gain clearance through the OEMS prior to beginning any classes. The license candidate shall complete the current National Standard Curriculum approved by the Board.

01-160.title: Registered Paramedic
01-160.description: The license candidate shall be 18 years of age within 1 year of the course completion date of the entry level course. Candidate must be a high school graduate or have a GED equivalent, or have completed a high school dual enrollment course. The license candidate shall meet the essential functions of an EMSP as outlined in the Functional Job Analysis. The Functional Job Analysis was developed and adopted for the State examination accommodations to meet the requirements of the ADA. A copy of these functions may be reviewed in the U.S. Department of Transportation, National Highway Traffic Safety Administration’s Emergency Medical Technician: EMT, National Standard Curriculum: Appendix A. The license candidate shall disclose any convictions during enrollment procedures and gain clearance through the OEMS prior to beginning any classes. The license candidate shall complete the current National Standard Curriculum approved by the Board.

01-122.title: Licensed Esthetician
01-122.description: Applicants meet the following qualifications: Is at least 16 years old; Has successfully completed at least 10 grades in secondary school, or equivalent; Has successfully completed at least 1,000 clock hours of licensed skin care instruction/registered school of esthetics/school of cosmetology; or 2,000 hours under immediate supervision of a continuously licensed esthetician under the provisions of the board, for 5 years before applying for apprenticeship.
01-122.agency: Alabama State Board of Cosmetology & Barbering

01-177.title: Licensed Eyebrow Threader
01-177.description: Applicants meet the following qualifications: Is at least 16 years old; Has successfully completed at least 10 grades in secondary school, or equivalent; Has successfully completed at least 1,000 clock hours of licensed skin care instruction/registered school of esthetics/school of cosmetology; or 2,000 hours under immediate supervision of a continuously licensed esthetician under the provisions of the board, for 5 years before applying for apprenticeship.
01-177.agency: Alabama State Board of Cosmetology & Barbering

01-11.title: Licensed Personal Financial Advisor
01-11.description: To become licensed in the State of Alabama, the applicant must have a $10,000 net worth or a surety bond of $50,000, an audited or attested balance sheet prepared with GAAP standards within the last 90 days; Applicants must successfully pass the required qualification examination.

00-FinOpL.title: Series 39 - Direct Participation Programs Limited Principal
00-FinOpL.description: Covered supervisory activities and products include regulatory compliance over sales of: ?Direct participation program limited partnerships (e.g., real estate, oil and gas, and equipment leasing) ?Limited liability companies ?S corporations In addition to sales supervision, the Series 39 qualifies a principal for the overall supervision of a firm’s investment banking and securities business—including compliance, underwriting and advertising—for those activities specially covered by each supervisory principal’s license.

01-163.title: Certified Alabama Smoke Diver
01-163.description: This applicant should be at least 18 years of age; possess a High School Diploma/GED; Complete the Physical Statement (AFC & PSC Form 05) form signed by an Alabama licensed physician or such designee; Successfully complete the Candidate Physical Ability Test (CPAT) within 12 months of start date; Prior to certification as a Fire Fighter I/II, certification to the Hazardous Materials/WMD Awareness and Operations levels is required.

01-164.title: Certified Career Fire Fighter
01-164.description: This applicant should be at least 18 years of age; possess a High School Diploma/GED; Complete the Physical Statement (AFC & PSC Form 05) form signed by an Alabama licensed physician or such designee; Successfully complete the Candidate Physical Ability Test (CPAT) within 12 months of start date; Prior to certification as a Fire Fighter I/II, certification to the Hazardous Materials/WMD Awareness and Operations levels is required.

01-165.title: Certified Rescue Officer I, II, III, IV
01-165.description: This applicant should be at least 18 years of age; possess a High School Diploma/GED; Complete the Physical Statement (AFC & PSC Form 05) form signed by an Alabama licensed physician or such designee; Successfully complete the Candidate Physical Ability Test (CPAT) within 12 months of start date; Prior to certification as a Fire Fighter I/II, certification to the Hazardous Materials/WMD Awareness and Operations levels is required.

01-39.title: Licensed Polygraph Examiner
01-39.description: A polygraph examiner must be 21 years of age, a citizen of the United States with no criminal background. Applicant must hold a baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university or, in lieu thereof, have five consecutive years of active investigative experience immediately preceding his application for polygraph licensing. He/She must have attended a Board approved polygraph examiners’ course and satisfactorily completed not less than six months of internship training. He/She must pass the Board’s polygraph examiners licensing examination at the conclusion of his internship. A licensed examiner is required to obtain at least 12 hours of continuing education yearly. The minimum standard for polygraph examinations: A pre-test interview, chart examination, and a post-test interview.

01-35.title: Registered Forester
01-35.description: This applicant must be a person of good character and reputation; Hold a bachelors or higher degree from a school approved by the board or accredited by the Society of American Foresters in a forestry curriculum accepted by the board; Have passed a written or oral examination, or both, designed to show the knowledge and skill obtained through graduation from the school or college; Have a specific record of two years or more of experience in the practice of forestry of a nature satisfactory to the board and indicating that the applicant is competent to practice forestry; Be a citizen of the United States or, if not a citizen of the United States a person who is legally in the United States with appropriate documentation from the federal government.
01-35.agency: Alabama State Board of Registration for Foresters

01-117.title: Licensed Funeral Director
01-117.description: This applicant should be at least 18 years of age and a citizen of the United States; Be a high school graduate or hold an equivalent diploma; Have served as an apprentice under the supervision of a licensed funeral director for at least two (2) years; Have a certificate of completion from an accredited Mortuary school or funeral service school as having completed a course of instruction in Funeral Arts or have a bachelor degree from an accredited post-secondary institution; Pass an examination.

01-36.title: Professional Geologist
01-36.description: To be eligible for a license as a professional geologist, the applicant must: be a U.S. citizen or provide proof of lawful presence; be a college graduate with a major in geology, engineering geology, or a related geological science; must have a minimum of 30 semester hours of course work in geological science. A “certified written reference or certified transcript from the college or university must be submitted directly to the Board; have at least five (5) years full-time professional geological work experience after receipt of a bachelor’s degree; All applicants are required to pass the written Practice of Geology Examination administered by the Alabama Board of Licensure for Professional Geologists.
01-36.agency: Alabama Board of Licensure for Professional Geologists

01-93.title: Certified Nurse Midwife (CNM)
01-93.description: All applicants shall: Be at least 21 years old; Be required to demonstrate United States citizenship or legal presence; Hold current unencumbered licensure as a registered nurse (RN) in Alabama; Graduate from a nurse midwifery program approved by the Accreditation Commission Midwifery Education (ACME) Of the American College of Nurse Midwives; Hold a master’s or higher degree in nursing; the Alabama Board of Nursing (ABN) may waive this requirement; Hold current certification as a nurse midwife by the American Midwifery Certification Board; Enrollment in the American College of Nurse Midwives Continuing Competency Assessment Program; Apply for approval of collaborative practice with a duly licensed physician actively engaged in the practice of obstetrics and gynecology.

01-7.title: Licensed Nursing Home Administrator
01-7.description: A nursing home administrator means any individual responsible for planning, organizing, directing and controlling the operation of a nursing home, or who in fact performs such functions, whether or not such functions are shared by one or more other persons. Only an individual who has qualified as a licensed and registered nursing home administrator and holds a valid current registration certificate may hold this job.
01-7.agency: Alabama Board of Examiners of Nursing Home Administrators

01-45.title: Licensed Independent Clinical Social Worker (LICSW)
01-45.description: Applicants must have a master of social work or a doctor of social work degree from a college or university approved or accredited by the Council on Social Work Education and hold a current LMSW license; Applicants must have received two (2) years or more of postgraduate continuing supervision provided by an LICSW prior to application for the LICSW exam. Candidate must pass an exam as prescribed by the Board. Applicants must be able to exercise independent judgment and demonstrate skill and interventions directly related to individuals, families, groups, communities, or organizations. In at least one of these client groups, the LICSW shall demonstrate in-depth knowledge and skills. The LICSW should be able to employ practice theory and research findings in all aspects of their practice.
01-45.agency: Alabama State Board of Social Workers Examiners

01-47.title: Licensed Master Social Worker (LMSW)
01-47.description: Applicants should contact the Alabama State Board of Social Work Examiners for qualifications and requirements.
01-47.agency: Alabama State Board of Social Workers Examiners

01-103.title: Licensed Hearing Aid Specialist (LHAS)
01-103.description: To become licensed, an applicant must be at least 19 years of age; Be of good moral character; Have an education equivalent to a four-year course in an accredited high school; Is free of contagious or infectious disease; Is a citizen of the United States or, if not a citizen of the United States, a person who is legally present in the United States with appropriate documentation from the federal government. All applicants must first complete the proper apprenticeship program. To be accepted into the apprentice program applicants must be sponsored by a licensed Hearing Aid Dispenser. Apprentice must complete a distance learning course and pay all applicable fees. An applicant who meets the qualifications of subsection (a) as determined by the board who applies for license by examination shall appear at a time, place, and before such persons as the board may designate to be examined by means of written and practical tests in order to demonstrate that he or she is qualified to practice the fitting and sale of hearing instruments.
01-103.agency: State of Alabama Hearing Instrument Dealers Board

01-48.title: Licensed Assistant Behavior Analyst
01-48.description: To become a licensed behavior analyst assistant applicants must: Be of good moral character and pass a state approved background check; Earn at least a Bachelor's Degree in Behavior Analysis; Complete an undergraduate-level certification program; Pass the BCBA Certification Exam.

01-139.title: Licensed HVAC Contractor
01-139.description: The applicant must be a U.S. citizen or provide proof of being lawfully authorized to be present in the United States. To become a certified heating and air conditioning contractor in the State of Alabama, the applicant must have knowledge of the trade evidenced by passing a written examination. An applicant for the heating, air conditioning, or refrigeration certified contractor license shall be eligible to sit for the examination if the applicant has held an apprentice registration, issued by this Board for two or more calendar years; or has completed 3,000 hours of coursework or experience, as defined by the Board; or is an graduate of an approved heating, air conditioning, or refrigeration curriculum.
01-139.agency: Alabama Board of Heating,Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Contractors

01-189.title: Licensed Refrigeration Contractor
01-189.description: The applicant must be a U.S. citizen or provide proof of being lawfully authorized to be present in the United States. To become a certified heating and air conditioning contractor in the State of Alabama, the applicant must have knowledge of the trade evidenced by passing a written examination. An applicant for the heating, air conditioning, or refrigeration certified contractor license shall be eligible to sit for the examination if the applicant has held an apprentice registration, issued by this Board for two or more calendar years; or has completed 3,000 hours of coursework or experience, as defined by the Board; or is an graduate of an approved heating, air conditioning, or refrigeration curriculum.
01-189.agency: Alabama Board of Heating,Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Contractors

00-Ins.title: NIPR Insurance Registry
00-Ins.description: Licensed Insurance Occupations must also be registered at the federal level.

01-64.title: Registered Interior Designer
01-64.description: The applicant must meet the following requirements to become registered: Be of good ethical character; Either satisfy all educational and experience requirements to take the National Council for Interior Design Qualification (NCIDQ) examination; OR hold a degree from a National Architectural Accreditation Board (NAAB) accredited school, or is a registered architect, who satisfies eligibility requirements to take the NCIDQ examination; Passed the NCIDQ examination; Be at least 21 years of age.
01-64.agency: Alabama Board for Registered Interior Designers

01-65.title: Licensed Sign Language Interpreter & Transliterator
01-65.description: To become an interpreter in the State of Alabama, an applicant is required to have certain nationally recognized credentials. Those interested in being Licensed must submit a current Certified Registry for the Deaf (RID) membership card. Those interested in being Permitted must submit proof of passing an RID approved ethics or written knowledge exam and one of several approved performance assessment tests. Individuals who do not qualify for a License or a Permit may apply for a Provisional Permit, which is valid for one year only and within that year those Permit holders must pass approved tests in order to upgrade to a permanent status.
01-65.agency: Alabama Licensure Board for Interpreters & Transliterators

01-52.title: Alabama Professional Educator Certificate
01-52.description: Teacher certification applicants must: be of good moral character; Present evidence of successful completion of at least a bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited institution of higher education; Present evidence of successful completion of a Board approved teacher education program or be a participant in an Alabama alternative certification program; and, Pass the required Alabama (ABI) AND Federal Bureaus of Investigation (FBI) background clearance checks; Passing scores on PRAXIS Tests and Assessments.

01-14.title: Licensed Landscape Architect
01-14.description: An applicant must submit evidence that the applicant has completed the course of study in and graduated from a college or school of landscape architecture approved by the Board. The applicant also must submit evidence of actual practical experience in landscape architectural work of a grade and character satisfactory to the Board. A total six years of combined education and experience must be completed before an applicant may apply for examination. Each year of study in an approved college or school of landscape architecture will be accepted as one year of such combined education and experience for a maximum of five years. A master’s or doctoral degree in landscape architecture shall fulfill the requirements for five years combined education and practical experience.

requirements.label: Exam
requirements.value: Both state and third-party exams required

01-14.agency: Alabama Board of Examiners of Landscape Architects

01-157.title: Professional Landscape Designer Operator (LD)
01-157.description: An applicant must submit evidence that the applicant has completed the course of study in and graduated from a college or school of landscape architecture approved by the Board. The applicant also must submit evidence of actual practical experience in landscape architectural work of a grade and character satisfactory to the Board. A total six years of combined education and experience must be completed before an applicant may apply for examination. Each year of study in an approved college or school of landscape architecture will be accepted as one year of such combined education and experience for a maximum of five years. A master’s or doctoral degree in landscape architecture shall fulfill the requirements for five years combined education and practical experience.

requirements.label: Exam
requirements.value: Both state and third-party exams required

01-157.agency: Alabama Board of Examiners of Landscape Architects

01-169.title: Professional Ornamental & Turf Pest Control Opeartor (OTPS)
01-169.description: In order to become a licensed landscape designer or planter in the State of Alabama, the applicant must: have sufficient knowledge and competency to do the work, but no formal education is required; submit an exam application and a written statement outlining their training and experience in this field; pass a written examination and obtain a Professional Services Permit and Nursery Dealer Permit in this field; pass a written examination and obtain a Professional Services Permit and Nursery Dealer Permit.

01-49.title: Licensed Attorney at Law
01-49.description: The applicant must be at least 19 years of age; Have high moral character evidenced by an investigation by the Alabama State Bar and approval by a committee on character and fitness prior to being admitted to the Alabama State Bar; Be a graduate of a law school approved by the American Bar Association or 1 of 2 non-accredited schools located in Alabama.

requirements.label: Exam
requirements.value: Both state and third-party exams required

01-38.title: Licensed Behavior Analyst
01-38.description: To become a licensed behavior analyst applicants must: Be of good moral character and pass a state approved background check; Earn at least a Master's Degree in Behavior Analysis; Complete a period of supervised practice; Pass the BCBA Certification Exam.

01-140.title: Certified Locksmith Qualifying Agent
01-140.description: The applicants must have completed Board approved locksmith certifications class and passed the proctored exam. 8 hours of continued competency is required annually.
01-140.agency: Alabama Electronic Security Board of Licensure

01-190.title: Certified Professional Locksmith/Access Control/CCTV Installer
01-190.description: The applicants must have completed Board approved locksmith certifications class and passed the proctored exam. 8 hours of continued competency is required annually.
01-190.agency: Alabama Electronic Security Board of Licensure

01-101.title: Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN)
01-101.description: All applicants shall: be required to demonstrate United States citizenship or legal presence; Be of good moral character; Be a high school graduate or the equivalent, as determined by the Board; Have successfully completed an approved practical nursing program of at least one (1) year in length; Pass the National Council Licensure Examination for Practical Nurses (NCLEX-PN); Those practical nurses already licensed in another state may apply for Alabama License by endorsement.

01-120.title: Licensed Manicurist
01-120.description: To be licensed as a manicurist the following qualifications must be satisfied: At least 16 years old; Has successfully completed at least 10 grades in secondary school, or equivalent; Successfully completed at least 750 clock hours of manicure instructions at a licensed/registered school or approved program; Pays examination fee.
01-120.agency: Alabama State Board of Cosmetology & Barbering

01-42.title: Licensed Marriage & Family Therapist
01-42.description: This applicant must be at least 19 years of age; Applicant shall be required to demonstrate his or her United States citizenship; Must complete a Master’s degree, plus two (2) years related work experience; Must complete a minimum two (2) years post-graduate supervision requirement. All applicants must meet education requirements, as well as supervision and intern hours; Applicants must pass an examination approved by the Board and monitor continuing education credits to maintain licensure.

requirements.label: Exam
requirements.value: Both state and third-party exams required

01-42.agency: Alabama Board of Examiners in Marriage & Family Therapists

01-41.title: Licensed Professional Counselor
01-41.description: Applicants should contact the Alabama State Department of Education licensing board for all applicable fees, requirements, qualification, and examinations.

01-107.title: Licensed Massage Therapist
01-107.description: This applicant should be at least 19 years of age and be a citizen of the United States; Must have successfully completed a minimum of 650 hours from an accredited massage therapy school and be certified by the National Certification Board for Therapeutic Massage and Bodywork; Applicants must pass the National Certification Board for Therapeutic Massage and Bodywork examination. Must provide certified transcripts and verification of their national certification; Must produce evidence of a $1,000,000 Personal Liability Insurance coverage, or hold a license in another state where the standards of practice or licensure are equal to or more-strict than the State of Alabama. Every massage therapist licensed in Alabama shall be required to complete 16 hours of continuing education as a condition for renewing his or her license.

00-52.title: Assistant Engineer (Limited - Oceans)
00-52.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as an Assistant Engineer (Limited - Oceans) include 1,080 days at sea, with 540 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-52.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-47.title: First Assistant Engineer - Upper Level
00-47.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a First Assistant Engineer - Upper Level, the applicant must complete 360 days of service as a Second or Third Assistant Engineer; while holding a Second Assistant Engineer license. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations
00-47.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-49.title: Third Assistant Engineer - Upper Level
00-49.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Third Assistant Engineer (upper Level, the applicant must complete one of the following: 1080 days of service in the engine room with 720 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED); or 1080 days as a machinist apprentice engaged in construction or repair of marine, locomotive, or stationary engines plus 360 days of sea service in an engine room as oiler, watertender, or jr. engineer; or graduate from an approved course of studies. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-49.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

01-88.title: Licensed Respiratory Therapist
01-88.description: Applicants must be 18 years old, a high school graduate or equivalent and meet one of the following criteria: a. Hold credentials as a registered or certified respiratory therapist; b. Hold a temporary license and have passed the examination for CRT or RRT within one year of application; c. Have a valid RRT license from another state; Have been approved by the board as being qualified through special training equal or superior to standards established in Alabama by the board; e. Was employed in the administration of respiratory therapy under the direction of a physician with the effective date of the adoption of rules and regulations set by the board; Has submitted a completed application and payed all required fees.
01-88.agency: Alabama State Board of Respiratory Therapist

01-46.title: Certified Advanced Alcohol & Drug Counselor (AADC)
01-46.description: Applicants should contact the Alabama State Board of Social Work Examiners for qualifications and requirements.
01-46.agency: Alabama State Board of Social Workers Examiners

01-136.title: Licensed Mine Boss
01-136.description: Applicants should contact the Alabama Department of Labor's Mine Safety and Inspection Unit for qualifications.

00-10.title: Nuclear Facility Operator
00-10.description: Nuclear Facility Operators are required to have either training or experience to become licensed. They must pass a medical exam, a written test, and an operating test. Although the license is granted for 6 years, licensees must pass another medical exam every two years and an operating test annually. Also, they must undergo requalification training while employed. Nuclear Facility Senior Operators have additional experience and pass another exam to be promoted from Nuclear Facility Operators. Further information can be found at the web site: http://www.nrc.gov/reactors/operator-licensing.html

01-92.title: Certified Registered Nurse Anesthetist (CRNA)
01-92.description: All applicants shall: be required to demonstrate United States citizenship or legal presence; Hold current unencumbered licensure as a registered nurse in Alabama; Hold a master’s degree, or post-master’s certificate in advanced practice nursing from an accredited graduate program in nurse anesthesia recognized by the Alabama Board of Nursing. The master’s degree is not required for graduates prior to 2003; Hold current certification as a Nurse Anesthetist by the National Board on Certification & Recertification of Nurse Anesthetists (NBCRNA) www. aana.com.

01-94.title: Certified Registered Nurse Practitioner (CRNP)
01-94.description: All applicants shall: be required to demonstrate United States citizenship or legal presence; Hold current unencumbered licensure as a registered nurse in Alabama; Hold a master’s degree, or post-master’s certificate in nursing from an accredited graduate program recognized by the Alabama Board of Nursing from a program designed to prepare clinical nurse specialists; Hold current certification by national certifying agency recognized by the Board in the specialty consistent with educational preparation as a clinical nurse specialist and appropriate to the area of practice

00-63.title: Hospital Corpsman
00-63.description: A Hospital Corpsman is a staff officer and is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). To obtain a COR requires completing first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training within the past 12 months and meeting medical fitness standards. A hospital corpsman must have U.S. military experience as and a rating of hospital corpsman or Health Services Technician or equivalent. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SUBPART=H&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-63.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

01-86.title: Licensed Occupational Therapist
01-86.description: This applicant shall: Be a citizen of the United States; Has successfully completed the academic requirements of an accredited educational program in Occupational Therapy as prescribed by the Board; Must pass a written examination administered by the National Board of Certification in Occupational Therapy.
01-86.agency: Alabama State Board of Occupational Therapy

01-73.title: Doctor of Optometry
01-73.description: An applicant should complete: application for examination; Official transcript from the various schools and colleges that you have obtained the following: Pre-optometry; minimum of three (3) years of professional study; Optometry Degree; four (4) years of professional study. Transcript must list the entrance and graduation dates. Proof of passing parts I and II of the examination administered by the National Board of Examiners in Optometry; After passing parts I and II, proof of passing part III of the examination administered by the National Board of Examiners in Optometry; Protocol furnished by the Board for the use of pharmaceutical agents in the treatment of the eye and its adjacent structures.

requirements.label: Exam
requirements.value: Both state and third-party exams required

01-192.title: Licensed Orthotic Fitter
01-192.description: Applicants should be a U.S. citizen; Filed a written application for approval; Applicants must meet one of the following requirements: a. Have a baccalaureate degree in orthotics and prosthetics and completed 1,900 hours per discipline of directed employment supervised under a certified/licensed instructor; b. Have a baccalaureate degree and successfully completed an approved post-baccalaureate certificate course and completed 1,900 hours per discipline of directed employment supervised under a certified/licensed instructor; Have an associate's degree and completed postsecondary coursework in anatomy, physiology, physics, biology, chemistry, algebra, and calculus and have worked under supervision of a certified/licensed instructor for not less than four consecutive years of the past six years in an accredited facility; Have successfully completed postsecondary coursework in anatomy, physiology, physics, biology, chemistry, algebra, and calculus and have worked under the supervision of a licensed/certified instructor for not less than eight years for the past 12 years and be certified as a orthotist, prosthetist, or prosthetist/orthotist.
01-192.agency: Alabama State Board of Prosthetists and Orthotist

01-102.title: Licensed Orthotist
01-102.description: The applicant must: be a U.S. citizen or provide verification that applicant is authorized to work in the U.S. as proven by the U.S. Immigration and Naturalization Board; Be of good moral character; meet one (1) of the following educational requirements from an accredited college or university: Bachelor’s Degree in Orthotics and Prosthetics, Bachelor’s Degree plus a certificate in Orthotics or Prosthetics, Associate’s Degree including Specific Coursework Hours, Post-Secondary Coursework in Specific Course Hours; Applicant will be required to submit notarized Attestation of Experience Providing Comprehensive Orthotic Care Form and/or Attestation of Experience Providing Comprehensive Prosthetic Care Form; All new applicants must have taken and passed either the BOC or ABC exam in their discipline to be considered for licensure. A copy of the certificate must be included in the application packet.
01-102.agency: Alabama State Board of Prosthetists and Orthotist

01-161.title: Licensed Prosthetist
01-161.description: The applicant must: be a U.S. citizen or provide verification that applicant is authorized to work in the U.S. as proven by the U.S. Immigration and Naturalization Board; Be of good moral character; meet one (1) of the following educational requirements from an accredited college or university: Bachelor’s Degree in Orthotics and Prosthetics, Bachelor’s Degree plus a certificate in Orthotics or Prosthetics, Associate’s Degree including Specific Coursework Hours, Post-Secondary Coursework in Specific Course Hours; Applicant will be required to submit notarized Attestation of Experience Providing Comprehensive Orthotic Care Form and/or Attestation of Experience Providing Comprehensive Prosthetic Care Form; All new applicants must have taken and passed either the BOC or ABC exam in their discipline to be considered for licensure. A copy of the certificate must be included in the application packet.
01-161.agency: Alabama State Board of Prosthetists and Orthotist

01-162.title: Licensed Prosthetist/Orthotist
01-162.description: The applicant must: be a U.S. citizen or provide verification that applicant is authorized to work in the U.S. as proven by the U.S. Immigration and Naturalization Board; Be of good moral character; meet one (1) of the following educational requirements from an accredited college or university: Bachelor’s Degree in Orthotics and Prosthetics, Bachelor’s Degree plus a certificate in Orthotics or Prosthetics, Associate’s Degree including Specific Coursework Hours, Post-Secondary Coursework in Specific Course Hours; Applicant will be required to submit notarized Attestation of Experience Providing Comprehensive Orthotic Care Form and/or Attestation of Experience Providing Comprehensive Prosthetic Care Form; All new applicants must have taken and passed either the BOC or ABC exam in their discipline to be considered for licensure. A copy of the certificate must be included in the application packet.
01-162.agency: Alabama State Board of Prosthetists and Orthotist

01-105.title: Licensed Occupational Therapist Assistant
01-105.description: An applicant for licensure as an occupational therapy assistant shall be a citizen of the United States or a person who is legally present in the United States with appropriate documentation from the federal government, and shall file a written application on forms provided by the board, showing to the satisfaction of the board fulfillment of all of the following requirements: Evidence of satisfactory and successful completion of all academic requirements for degree or certificate conferral from an education program in occupational therapy recognized by the board and accredited by the Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education of the American Occupational Therapy Association, Incorporated.; Applicant shall pass an examination to test his or her knowledge of the basic clinical sciences related to occupational therapy, and occupational therapy theory and practice, the applicants professional skills and judgment in the utilization of occupational therapy techniques and methods, and such other subjects as the board may deem useful to determine the applicant's fitness to practice.
01-105.agency: Alabama State Board of Occupational Therapy

01-112.title: Professional Fumigation Pest Control Operator (FC)
01-112.description: The applicant shall submit a written statement outlying their training and experience in professional work or services. The applicant must provide evidence of education and/or work experience to the Department of Agriculture and must pass a written examination (exam offered four (4) times per year). Ornamental & Turf Pest Control companies must obtain a Professional Services permit.

01-167.title: Professional Horticulture Pest Control Operator
01-167.description: The applicant shall submit a written statement outlying their training and experience in professional work or services. The applicant must provide evidence of education and/or work experience to the Department of Agriculture and must pass a written examination (exam offered four (4) times per year). Ornamental & Turf Pest Control companies must obtain a Professional Services permit.

01-168.title: Professional Household, Institutional & Industrial Pest Control Operator (HPC)
01-168.description: The applicant shall submit a written statement outlying their training and experience in professional work or services. The applicant must provide evidence of education and/or work experience to the Department of Agriculture and must pass a written examination (exam offered four (4) times per year). Ornamental & Turf Pest Control companies must obtain a Professional Services permit.

01-74.title: Licensed Pharmacist
01-74.description: Applicant must: be 19 years of age or older; Be of good moral character; Be a U.S. citizen or provide verification that applicant is authorized to work in the U.S. as proven by the U.S. Immigration and Naturalization Board; Hold a professional degree from a division, school, college or university department of pharmacy recognized by the ACPE, American Council on Pharmaceutical Education; Have completed an approved practical training program of 1,500 hours under the supervision of a licensed preceptor in a pharmacy recognized by the board as qualified for training pharmacy externs and interns; Present proof of the completion of these practical training requirements by affidavit from the preceptor under whom training is served.

requirements.label: Exam
requirements.value: Both state and third-party exams required

01-98.title: Licensed Pharmacist Technician
01-98.description: Applicant must: be 19 years of age or older; Be of good moral character; Be a U.S. citizen or provide verification that applicant is authorized to work in the U.S. as proven by the U.S. Immigration and Naturalization Board; Have submitted a written applicant to the Secretary of the Board.

01-87.title: Licensed Physical Therapist
01-87.description: This applicant must: be of good moral character; Be a U.S. citizen or provide verification that applicant is authorized to work in the U.S. as proven by the U.S. Immigration and Naturalization Board; Be a graduate of a Board-approved Program of Physical Therapy Education; Pass a written examination approved by the Board.

00-80.title: Marine Physician Assistant
00-80.description: A Marine Physician Assistant is a staff officer and is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). To obtain a COR requires completing first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training within the past 12 months and meeting medical fitness standards. A physician assistant must also have training as a physician's assistant or nurse practitioner. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SUBPART=H&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-80.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

01-83.title: Board Certified Anesthesiological Assistant
01-83.description: Interested parties should visit the Alabama Board of Medicall Examiners for qualifications and requirements.
01-83.agency: Alabama State Board of Medical Examiners

01-159.title: Board Certified Physician Assistant
01-159.description: Interested parties should visit the Alabama Board of Medicall Examiners for qualifications and requirements.
01-159.agency: Alabama State Board of Medical Examiners

01-84.title: Board Certified Physician Assistant
01-84.description: Aplplicant must provide evidence, satisfactory to the Board, of successful completion of a training program accredited by the Committee on Allied Health Education and Accreditation (CAHEA), or the Commission on Accreditation of Allied Health Education Programs (CAAHEP), or their successor agencies. Must provide evidence, satisfactory to the Board, of successful completion of the Certifying Examination for Anesthesiologist Assistants (CEAA) as administered by the National Commission for Certification of Anesthesiologist Assistants (NCCAA). Applications must be submitted to the board, pay all required application fees, submit to a criminal background check, provide fingerprints and pay criminal background check fee.
01-84.agency: Alabama State Board of Medical Examiners

00-31.title: Tankerman
00-31.description: Tankerman refers to several endorsements or qualified ratings to Merchant Marine Documents (MMD). All Tankerman endorsements require qualifying experience, training in firefighting and cargo (dangerous liquids or liquefied gasses), and passing an exam. Endorsements include Tankerman - Person-In-Charge (Tankerman PIC), Tankerman-Engineer, Tankerman Assistant, and Tankerman - PIC (Barge). Tankerman endorsements are valid for the duration of the MMD, which is issued for 5 years. Renewal of certification requires meeting all the requirements to renew the MMD and either have recent qualifying experience or training. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR13.109) at website http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr13_02.html.
00-31.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

01-130.title: Certified Journeyman Gas Fitter
01-130.description: Applicant must: be at least 16 years of age or possess a work permit; Be of good moral character; Be a U.S. citizen or provide verification that applicant is authorized to work in the U.S. as proven by the U.S. Immigration and Naturalization Board; A journeyman's plumber or gas fitter applicant shall submit proof that the applicant has two (2) years of work experience as an apprentice plumber or gas fitter or has completed an apprentice training program approved by the board; A master plumber or gas fitter applicant shall submit proof that the applicant has one (1) year of work experience as an journeyman plumber or gas fitter; Applicants for journeyman plumber or gas fitter shall be examined, orally or in writing, upon the fundamentals of plumbing or gas fitting, the theory and practice of plumbing installation and construction or gas fitting work, and the experience and ability of the applicant in practical plumbing installation and construction or gas fitting work; Must possess sufficient education and/or experience as a registered apprentice to pass the journeyman examination.
01-130.agency: Alabama Plumbers and Gas Fitters Examining Board

01-181.title: Certified Journeyman Plumber
01-181.description: Applicant must: be at least 16 years of age or possess a work permit; Be of good moral character; Be a U.S. citizen or provide verification that applicant is authorized to work in the U.S. as proven by the U.S. Immigration and Naturalization Board; A journeyman's plumber or gas fitter applicant shall submit proof that the applicant has two (2) years of work experience as an apprentice plumber or gas fitter or has completed an apprentice training program approved by the board; A master plumber or gas fitter applicant shall submit proof that the applicant has one (1) year of work experience as an journeyman plumber or gas fitter; Applicants for journeyman plumber or gas fitter shall be examined, orally or in writing, upon the fundamentals of plumbing or gas fitting, the theory and practice of plumbing installation and construction or gas fitting work, and the experience and ability of the applicant in practical plumbing installation and construction or gas fitting work; Must possess sufficient education and/or experience as a registered apprentice to pass the journeyman examination.
01-181.agency: Alabama Plumbers and Gas Fitters Examining Board

01-182.title: Certified Master Gas Fitter
01-182.description: Applicant must: be at least 16 years of age or possess a work permit; Be of good moral character; Be a U.S. citizen or provide verification that applicant is authorized to work in the U.S. as proven by the U.S. Immigration and Naturalization Board; A journeyman's plumber or gas fitter applicant shall submit proof that the applicant has two (2) years of work experience as an apprentice plumber or gas fitter or has completed an apprentice training program approved by the board; A master plumber or gas fitter applicant shall submit proof that the applicant has one (1) year of work experience as an journeyman plumber or gas fitter; Applicants for journeyman plumber or gas fitter shall be examined, orally or in writing, upon the fundamentals of plumbing or gas fitting, the theory and practice of plumbing installation and construction or gas fitting work, and the experience and ability of the applicant in practical plumbing installation and construction or gas fitting work; Must possess sufficient education and/or experience as a registered apprentice to pass the journeyman examination.
